physics_goals.quote: We report an improved measurement of the free neutron lifetime $\tau_{n}$ using the UCN$\tau$ apparatus at the Los Alamos Neutron Science Center.
physics_goals.value: Measure the free neutron lifetime with ultracold neutrons stored in a magneto-gravitational trap and detected in situ

summary.plain: An experiment at Los Alamos that holds ultracold neutrons in a bowl made of magnets and gravity, so they cannot touch any walls, and counts how many survive. Its measured neutron lifetime is about 877.8 seconds, with an uncertainty of about 0.3 seconds. An upgrade is underway.
summary.technical: UCNtau at the Los Alamos Ultra Cold Neutron Facility (LANSCE): asymmetric magneto-gravitational trap with in situ detection of surviving UCN; tau_n = 877.75 ± 0.28 stat +0.22/-0.16 syst s (2017-2018 data), all-data average 877.82 ± 0.22 (stat) +0.20/-0.17 (syst) s including 2020-2022 runs. Upgrade underway as of June 2025.
